visa.name: Partner visa (offshore, de facto) — temporary 309 then permanent 100
visa.onshore_alternative: 820/801 (use if the applicant is in Australia at lodgement)
visa.fee_note: As of July 2026. Non-refundable even if refused or withdrawn. Verify current fee at immi.homeaffairs.gov.au before lodging.
visa.lodgement: Online only via ImmiAccount. One combined application covers both 309 and 100.
key_rules: Applicant must be outside Australia when the 309 is lodged AND when it is granted. They may visit Australia on a separate visitor visa during processing, but must depart before the visa is decided.
No bridging visa — offshore applicants have no automatic right to be in or stay in Australia while the application is processed.

De facto: 12 months living together immediately before applying, OR a child of the relationship. (Relationship registration usually can't waive the 12 months for offshore couples, as Australian state/territory registers generally require local residency — rely on 12 months cohabitation or compelling/compassionate circumstances instead.)
April 2026 change: lodge 'decision-ready'. Include all documents up front; expect limited/no follow-up requests; incomplete applications risk faster refusal.
Both applicant and sponsor must provide police clearances for every country lived in 12+ months since age 16.
Do NOT book the health examination until instructed via ImmiAccount after lodgement.
visa.disclaimer: This tool organises documents and reproduces publicly available guidance. It is not migration advice. Confirm everything against immi.homeaffairs.gov.au and consider a MARA-registered migration agent for anything non-standard.

items.title: Confirm de facto basis met
items.guidance: 12 months cohabitation immediately before applying, OR a child of the relationship, OR compelling/compassionate circumstances. Registration usually can't waive the 12 months for offshore couples. Record which one you rely on.

items.title: Applicant is outside Australia at time of application
items.guidance: The 309 must be lodged while the applicant is offshore. Note current country of residence.

items.title: Applicant will be outside Australia when the visa is granted
items.guidance: For the 309, the applicant must be offshore at the moment of grant. If visiting Australia during processing, plan to depart before a decision is expected.

items.title: Sponsor eligibility & sponsorship limits
items.guidance: Sponsor must be an Australian citizen, PR, or eligible NZ citizen; must not have sponsored 2+ partners previously; and must not have been sponsored as a partner within the last 5 years.

items.title: Applicant passport (photo/bio page)
items.guidance: Valid passport. Include all pages showing identity and any name changes.

items.title: Applicant birth certificate
items.guidance: Certified translation if not in English.

items.title: Applicant passport-style photo
items.guidance: Recent, meets DHA photo specs.

items.title: Change-of-name / prior identity documents
items.guidance: Only if the applicant has changed name or held other identity documents.

items.title: Proof sponsor is Australian citizen / PR / eligible NZ citizen
items.guidance: Australian passport, citizenship certificate, or visa grant showing PR/eligible NZ status.

items.title: Sponsor birth certificate / photo ID
items.guidance: Supports identity on Form 40SP.

items.title: Joint bank account statements
items.guidance: Statements over time carry the most weight. Show ongoing joint use, not a token account.

items.title: Joint liabilities (loans, credit, insurance)
items.guidance: Joint loans, shared insurance policies, one partner named on the other's policy.

items.title: Shared household bills / utilities in both names
items.guidance: Electricity, gas, water, internet, phone showing both names or the same address.

items.title: Joint ownership of major assets
items.guidance: Property, vehicle, or other significant shared assets.

items.title: Evidence of how you share finances / support each other
items.guidance: Transfers between accounts, one supporting the other, shared budgeting.

items.title: Joint lease or mortgage / property documents
items.guidance: Both names on the tenancy or title. If only one name, explain in statements and support with other household evidence.

items.title: Mail addressed to both at the same address
items.guidance: A spread of correspondence over time to the shared address.

items.title: Utility / service accounts at shared address
items.guidance: Accounts, connection notices, or council correspondence tied to the home.

items.title: Statement on division of household responsibilities
items.guidance: Who does what — chores, finances, care duties. Usually covered in personal statements.

items.title: Shared responsibility for children / dependants (if any)
items.guidance: Only if applicable.

items.title: Photos together across the relationship timeline
items.guidance: Dated where possible: with family/friends, events, travel, over time — not just one occasion.

items.title: Joint travel evidence
items.guidance: Bookings, itineraries, boarding passes showing travel as a couple.

items.title: Joint invitations / events / memberships
items.guidance: Invitations addressed to both, shared club/gym memberships, joint bookings.

items.title: Evidence you present publicly as a couple
items.guidance: Social media, messages to/from friends and family acknowledging the relationship.

items.title: Communication history during any separations
items.guidance: Messages/calls when apart, showing a continuing relationship.

items.title: Evidence of future plans together
items.guidance: Wills naming each other, superannuation/insurance beneficiaries, joint long-term commitments.

items.title: Relationship history timeline
items.guidance: How and when you met, key milestones, when cohabitation began, decision to commit. Feeds both personal statements.

items.title: Applicant's personal statement
items.guidance: First-person account of the relationship across all four pillars. The AI drafter can build a first pass from your timeline.

items.title: Sponsor's personal statement
items.guidance: The sponsor's own first-person account — should corroborate, not copy, the applicant's.

items.title: Form 888 statutory declaration #1
items.guidance: From an Australian citizen or PR (16+) who knows you as a couple. Witnessed correctly.

items.title: Form 888 statutory declaration #2
items.guidance: A second independent witness. More strong 888s = stronger social/commitment evidence.

items.title: Sponsor application (Form 40SP)
items.guidance: Lodged by the sponsor through their own ImmiAccount at the same time as the main application.

items.title: Sponsor AFP National Police Check (Code 33)
items.guidance: Australian Federal Police check submitted as part of Form 40SP.

items.title: Health examination (after lodgement)
items.guidance: Do NOT book before lodging. Complete with a DHA-approved panel physician — normally in the country where the applicant is living. If the applicant happens to be visiting Australia when instructed, Bupa Medical Visa Services handles these in Australia. Book only once instructed through ImmiAccount.

items.title: Applicant police clearances (all relevant countries)
items.guidance: One for every country lived in 12+ months since age 16. Note each country and order early — some take weeks.

items.title: Sponsor police clearances
items.guidance: Sponsor also provides clearances for countries lived in 12+ months since 16 (AFP check via Form 40SP covers Australia).

items.title: Form 80 (if requested / complex history)
items.guidance: Detailed personal particulars form — include if the applicant has extensive travel/residence history.

items.title: ImmiAccount created & application completed
items.guidance: Paper applications are not accepted.

items.title: Four-pillar readiness check passed
items.guidance: Every pillar has solid evidence before lodging. The dashboard gate enforces this.

items.title: Fee ready (AUD 11,710) & payment method
items.guidance: Non-refundable. Card surcharge applies. Confirm current fee before paying.

items.title: Decision-ready confirmation
items.guidance: Under the April 2026 approach, lodge only when complete — follow-up requests are limited and incomplete applications risk faster refusal.
